newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, U.S. arb demand fades.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, U.S. arb demand fades.

text.p: NWE fuel oil prices were steady on Tuesday, but many traders continued to see bullish fundamentals going into the winter.
High sulphur cargoes were supported by talk up to $120 cif NWE, but U.S. arbitrage interest faded as recent high prices there were not backed up by physical demand, traders said.
Low sulphur fundamentals were reasonably tight after Italy's 250,000-tonne buying spree last week and dealers expected an arbitrage to open from the Caribbean to the Mediterranean in December.
Traders said many Italian ports were now so congested that the country was unlikely to buy any more prompt supply, but they expected Italy to return to the market soon for pre-Christmas supply.
Three December-loading low sulphur cargoes were available from northern European refiners, and prices were stable at $132 fob, a Scandinavian trader said.
High sulphur barges traded steady at $118-120 fob ARA and low sulphur barges were sold at $132.50 fob Rotterdam.
